answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may earn fees or vote, then slash that bond when randomized audits expose coordinated fraud. A juniper agent might be assigned a private task, while a mirror market and a raven agent receive related but different tasks; copied identities tend to produce correlated answers. Creating thousands of Sybils therefore requires thousands of funded bonds, and one detected cluster can destroy the attacker’s capital and accumulated access.
